# core-kernel

> Zero-dependency TypeScript building blocks for DDD / Clean Architecture on Bun and Node ≥ 20 (ESM + CJS, TypeScript ≥ 5.4). Business rules return `Result<T, E>` with typed errors instead of throwing.

Rules an assistant must follow when writing code with core-kernel:

- Never throw for expected failures. Return `Result.fail(new XxxError(...))`. `throw` is only for API misuse or bugs.
- Read `result.value` / `result.error` only after narrowing: `if (r.isFail()) return r;` then `r.value`. `if (!r.ok)` also narrows.
- A `Fail<E>` can be returned as any `Result<U, E'>` when `E` is part of `E'`, so propagate failures with `return r`.
- Entities and value objects have a `private constructor` and a `static create(...)` returning `Result`. Entities also have `static restore(props, id)` for rehydration (no validation, no events).
- State changes only through domain methods that return `Result<void, ...>`. No setters, no public `props`.
- Repositories return `T | null` and throw on infrastructure failure. Use cases turn `null` into `NotFoundError`. Extend `BaseUseCase` so thrown errors become `UnexpectedError`.
- Repositories hold writes + `findById` only. Screen/list reads go through query ports that return DTOs.
- Inject `Clock` instead of calling `new Date()` (current time) in use cases/domain. Pass `now` into domain methods; deriving dates from it (`new Date(now.getTime() + ms)`) is fine.
- Rules that need data outside the aggregate (limits, uniqueness): the use case loads the minimum (`count`/`exists` repository method) and a pure domain function decides.
- Depend on the narrowest port: `FindByIdRepository<Order> & UpdateRepository<Order>`, not a full CRUD interface.
- Use typed ids: `class OrderId extends UniqueId { declare private readonly __brand: "OrderId" }`.
- Check the ready-made value objects (`core-kernel/vo`, `core-kernel/vo/br`) before writing a new one. Their issue codes/messages can be replaced with `{ errors: { DEFAULT_CODE: { code, message } } }` (e.g. for another language).
- Use `map`/`flatMap` to transform values only. For side effects (changing entity state), return early on failure and then mutate: `const v = check(); if (v.isFail()) return v; this.props.x = ...; return Result.ok();`.
- Libraries built on core-kernel (published packages, not apps): list it as a `peerDependency` (plus `devDependency`), keep it external in the bundle (`bun build --packages external`, or `external: ["core-kernel"]`), build declarations with `module`/`moduleResolution` `NodeNext` and `.js` extensions on relative imports (with `bundler` resolution the published `.d.ts` break for Node consumers), and check the package with `attw --pack . --profile node16`. Never use `postinstall` for git hooks (use `prepare`).

## Imports

- `core-kernel`: Result, Ok, Fail, AppError, ErrorKind, ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError, ForbiddenError, UnexpectedError, isAppError, Guard, ValueObject, isValueObject, Entity, isEntity, AggregateRoot, UniqueId, IdGenerator, DomainEvent, createDomainEvent, Auditable, UseCase, BaseUseCase, CreateRepository, UpdateRepository, DeleteRepository, FindByIdRepository, CrudRepository, EntityId, Clock, systemClock, DomainEventPublisher, Mapper, PaginatedInputDTO, PaginationMetaDTO, PaginatedResultDTO, validatePagination, toPaginatedResult
- `core-kernel/vo`: Email, Text, Url, Money, DateRange, StrongPassword
- `core-kernel/vo/br`: Cpf, Cnpj (numeric and alphanumeric, IN RFB 2.229/2024)
- `core-kernel/testing`: InMemoryRepository, FixedClock, SequentialIdGenerator, InMemoryEventPublisher, assertOk, assertFail

## Result

```ts nocheck
type Result<T, E extends AppError = AppError> = Ok<T, E> | Fail<E>;
Result.ok(value) / Result.ok()                     // Result<T, never> / Result<void, never>
Result.fail(error)                                 // Result<never, E>
r.isOk() / r.isFail() / r.ok                       // narrowing
r.map(fn) / r.flatMap(fn) / r.mapError(fn) / r.match({ ok, fail }) / r.unwrapOr(x)
r.unwrap()                                         // throws the error: tests and app edges only
Result.combine([a, b])                             // Result<[A, B], EA | EB>; merges ValidationError issues
Result.try(fn, mapError?) / Result.tryAsync(fn, mapError?)  // thrown → UnexpectedError (cause kept)
```

## Errors

```ts nocheck
new NotFoundError("Order not found", { code: "ORDER_NOT_FOUND", details?, cause? })
new ValidationError({ field: "email", code: "INVALID_EMAIL", message: "..." })   // or an array of issues
error.kind  // "validation" | "not_found" | "conflict" | "forbidden" | "unexpected" → adapters map to HTTP etc.
error.code  // stable machine-readable code; error.toJSON() for responses/logs
```

## Guard

All return `Result<void, ValidationError>` and accept `{ field?, code?, message? }`:
`required`, `notEmpty`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `inRange(value, { min?, max? })`, `integer`, `matches(value, regex)`, `oneOf(value, list)`.
`Guard.all([...])` accumulates every issue; `a.flatMap(() => b)` stops at the first failure.

Default issue codes: required `REQUIRED`, notEmpty `EMPTY`, minLength/maxLength `TOO_SHORT`/`TOO_LONG`, inRange `TOO_SMALL`/`TOO_LARGE`/`NOT_A_NUMBER`, integer `NOT_AN_INTEGER`, matches `INVALID_FORMAT`, oneOf `NOT_ALLOWED`. A `ValidationError` itself has code `VALIDATION_FAILED`; error defaults: `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `FORBIDDEN`, `UNEXPECTED` (override with specific codes).

## Ids

`XxxId.generate()` (UUID v4 by default; `UniqueId.useGenerator(g)` swaps it and returns a restore fn) and `XxxId.from(raw): Result<XxxId, ValidationError>` (any non-empty string, trimmed; empty → issue `INVALID_ID`, field `id`; override with `XxxId.from(raw, { field, code, message })`). Both return the subclass type.

## Value object template

```ts
// file: sku.vo.ts
import { Guard, type Result, type ValidationError, ValueObject } from "core-kernel";

export class Sku extends ValueObject<string> {
  private constructor(value: string) {
    super(value);
  }

  static create(raw: string, field = "sku"): Result<Sku, ValidationError> {
    const value = raw.trim().toUpperCase();
    return Guard.notEmpty(value, { field })
      .flatMap(() => Guard.matches(value, /^[A-Z0-9-]+$/, { field, code: "INVALID_SKU" }))
      .map(() => new Sku(value));
  }
}
```

`value` is deep-frozen; `equals` compares structure (same class only); `toJSON()` returns `value`.

## Aggregate template

```ts
// file: order.entity.ts
import {
  AggregateRoot,
  ConflictError,
  createDomainEvent,
  type DomainEvent,
  Result,
  UniqueId,
  type ValidationError,
} from "core-kernel";
import { Email } from "core-kernel/vo";

export class OrderId extends UniqueId {
  declare private readonly __brand: "OrderId";
}

export type OrderStatus = "pending" | "confirmed";

export interface OrderProps {
  customerEmail: Email;
  status: OrderStatus;
}

type OrderConfirmed = DomainEvent<"order.confirmed", { confirmedAt: string }>;

export class Order extends AggregateRoot<OrderProps, OrderId, OrderConfirmed> {
  private constructor(props: OrderProps, id: OrderId) {
    super(props, id);
  }

  static create(input: { customerEmail: string }): Result<Order, ValidationError> {
    return Email.create(input.customerEmail, { field: "customerEmail" }).map(
      (customerEmail) => new Order({ customerEmail, status: "pending" }, OrderId.generate()),
    );
  }

  static restore(props: OrderProps, id: OrderId): Order {
    return new Order(props, id);
  }

  get status(): OrderStatus {
    return this.props.status;
  }

  confirm(now: Date): Result<void, ConflictError> {
    if (this.props.status !== "pending") {
      return Result.fail(new ConflictError("Order is not pending", { code: "ORDER_NOT_PENDING" }));
    }
    this.props.status = "confirmed";
    this.addDomainEvent(
      createDomainEvent({
        name: "order.confirmed",
        aggregateId: this.id.value,
        occurredAt: now,
        payload: { confirmedAt: now.toISOString() },
      }),
    );
    return Result.ok();
  }
}
```

Entities are equal when they share class and id. `pullDomainEvents()` returns and clears pending events.

## Use case template

```ts
// file: confirm-order.usecase.ts
import {
  BaseUseCase,
  type Clock,
  type ConflictError,
  type DomainEventPublisher,
  type FindByIdRepository,
  NotFoundError,
  Result,
  type UpdateRepository,
  type ValidationError,
} from "core-kernel";
import { type Order, OrderId } from "./order.entity.js";

type ConfirmOrderError = ValidationError | NotFoundError | ConflictError;

export class ConfirmOrderUseCase extends BaseUseCase<{ orderId: string }, void, ConfirmOrderError> {
  constructor(
    private readonly orders: FindByIdRepository<Order> & UpdateRepository<Order>,
    private readonly events: DomainEventPublisher,
    private readonly clock: Clock,
  ) {
    super();
  }

  protected async handle({ orderId }: { orderId: string }): Promise<Result<void, ConfirmOrderError>> {
    const id = OrderId.from(orderId);
    if (id.isFail()) return id;
    const order = await this.orders.findById(id.value);
    if (!order) return Result.fail(new NotFoundError("Order not found", { code: "ORDER_NOT_FOUND" }));
    const confirmed = order.confirm(this.clock.now());
    if (confirmed.isFail()) return confirmed;
    await this.orders.update(order);
    await this.events.publish(order.pullDomainEvents());
    return Result.ok();
  }
}
// execute(input): Promise<Result<void, ConfirmOrderError | UnexpectedError>> — never rejects
```

## Testing template

```ts
// file: confirm-order.usecase.test.ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "bun:test";
import {
  assertFail,
  assertOk,
  FixedClock,
  InMemoryEventPublisher,
  InMemoryRepository,
} from "core-kernel/testing";
import { ConfirmOrderUseCase } from "./confirm-order.usecase.js";
import { Order } from "./order.entity.js";

const createSut = () => {
  const order = Order.create({ customerEmail: "ana@example.com" }).unwrap();
  const orders = new InMemoryRepository<Order>([order]);
  const events = new InMemoryEventPublisher();
  const useCase = new ConfirmOrderUseCase(orders, events, new FixedClock("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"));
  return { order, orders, events, useCase };
};

describe("ConfirmOrderUseCase", () => {
  it("confirms and publishes the event", async () => {
    const { order, events, useCase } = createSut();

    assertOk(await useCase.execute({ orderId: order.id.value }));
    expect(events.namesOf()).toEqual(["order.confirmed"]);
  });

  it("returns ORDER_NOT_FOUND for unknown ids", async () => {
    assertFail(await createSut().useCase.execute({ orderId: "missing" }), "ORDER_NOT_FOUND");
  });

  it("turns infrastructure errors into UnexpectedError", async () => {
    const { order, orders, useCase } = createSut();
    orders.failNext(new Error("db down"));

    assertFail(await useCase.execute({ orderId: order.id.value }), "UNEXPECTED");
  });
});
```

Other test helpers: `new SequentialIdGenerator("order").install()` makes ids predictable (event ids share the sequence; returns a restore function); `assertFail(result, code)` matches `error.code` or any validation issue code; `InMemoryRepository`: `new InMemoryRepository([...initial])`, `items`, `size`, `seed()`, `clear()`; `create` of a duplicate and `update` of a missing entity throw; extend it and use `this.find` / `this.filter` for custom queries (they honour `failNext`; if you read `this.store` directly, call `this.throwPendingFailure()` first).

## Skills, agents and checker

- Agent skills with detailed patterns ship in the package: `bunx core-kernel skills add` installs them into `.claude/skills` and/or `.agents/skills` (`skills update`, `skills check`). `ddd-migration` is the playbook for migrating a project to core-kernel.
- Subagents `ddd-architect` (model before coding, read-only), `ddd-reviewer` (review a diff, runs the checker) and `core-kernel-migrator`: `bunx core-kernel agents add` installs them into `.claude/agents` and/or `.codex/agents` (TOML).
- `core-kernel-check` (separate dev dependency) flags, with types, the mistakes that compile: typed id passed to an untyped parameter such as `pool.query(sql, [order.id])` (CK001, use `.value`), `AppError` handled as text (CK002, use `code`/`kind`), `try/catch` around `await useCase.execute()` (CK003, `execute` never rejects; the original exception is in `error.cause`), `throw`/`new Date()`/`unwrap()` in the domain or in `handle` (CK004–CK006), `result.map` used for side effects (CK007), `instanceof` on core-kernel errors (CK008). Run `bunx core-kernel-check` after editing and fix every finding.
- Claude Code plugin (skills, agents, and a hook that runs the checker on every edit): `claude plugin marketplace add macndesign/core-kernel` then `claude plugin install core-kernel@core-kernel`.
